messages.subject: Eclipse / StatET to R on Ubuntu on AWS?
messages.subject_clean: Eclipse / StatET to R on Ubuntu on AWS?
messages.body_plain:
If I want to access R running on Amazon AWS, in order to get access to 
more CPU and memory resource, what would be the best way to do that?

I know that this can be done in the case of another R development 
environment (RStudio) but I much prefer to use StatET if possible.

In other words, can I run StatET on my personal computer in Windows, and 
connect to R running remotely on say Ubuntu on AWS?

Or would it be better to run Eclipse and StatET also on the remote Ubunto 
instance and connect to it from my personal computer using X11 or some 
other remote access tool?

On Ubuntu, are there any particular approaches or sites you would 
recommend for approaches to installing R etc.?

In any case, thanks for the superb 3.4 or StatET with so many fixes and 
improvements!  I really appreciate that IDates are recognized now in the 
viewer, and that the issues with shortcuts have been fixed.

Best,

Don

messages.subject: Re: Eclipse / StatET to R on Ubuntu on AWS?
messages.subject_clean: Eclipse / StatET to R on Ubuntu on AWS?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Don,

If you add our repository

http://deb.openanalytics.eu/howto.html

you can use

sudo apt-get install architect-server

to install the server component of StatET on an Ubuntu machine in the cloud
(we support 12.04 and 14.04).

This will allow you to configure a so-called Remote R Console (ships with
standard StatET) and tunnel all traffic over SSH.

The remote command to use would be something along (adapt user home):

/opt/architect-server/stable/startup.sh "${address}" -wd="/home/tverbeke"

Best,
Tobias

P.S. For questions specific to Architect (which includes StatET), you can
ask questions at ask.openanalytics.eu

messages.subject: Keeping plot separate from "R Graphic view by StatET" and R-help window
messages.subject_clean: Keeping plot separate from "R Graphic view by StatET" and R-help window
messages.body_plain:
Hi guys,

Firstly, I’m loving the new StatET with Eclipse Luna. Thank you so much for that.

I switched from Windows 7 using Eclipse Kepler to Mac OS 10.9.5 using Eclipse Luna. I prefer to keep the R plot window separate from Eclipse and accomplish this by unchecking the box “Set R Graphic view by StatET as default graphic device for new plots in R” under the “R Console” tab in the configurations page. 

While that worked fine when I was using Kepler in Windows, it just brings up a blank window in Luna using Mac. I managed to get the plot to show when I use JRE 1.6 (rather than 1.8) but using the older JRE just opens the door to other issues. Any advice?

Also, the help window doesn’t appear to work correctly. Each time I type in “help(___)” where ___ is the name of a function, the R-help window tells me that there was “No help found on topic ___ in any package in the R library. Any advice on how to get it to show the help files? It works fine when I call up R in the terminal or the R gui. 

Thank you guys!

Linh
PhD Student
